resources.string: Detects which app is in the foreground so Zenith can show mindful messages and shields. Standard mode also reads browser address bars for website blocking and counts swipes in the short-video feeds you choose to limit. Limited mode receives only app-switch events and no screen or notification content. Zenith never records keystrokes.
Days in a row under your screen time target.
Streak for one app: shield stays under its limit, goal reaches its target.
Shows remaining time before daily screen time target.

Six chapters. One deliberate system.\n\nYou now know where the day lives, how to draw a boundary, how to interrupt autopilot, how to let the clock decide, how to read the mirror, and how to keep it all.

Usage history: tap a day to inspect it.
Top apps: the three biggest consumers today.
Your avatar is the door to level and achievements.
History becomes trustworthy after about three days.
This ring is today\'s screen time against your target. The flame is your current streak. You can tap the target anytime to change it.
Zenith gets sharper as it learns your patterns. Give it about three days before trusting the trend line.
A Shield blocks. A Goal rewards. Both appear in this list; tap one to open its app detail.
Bedtime, Alarm, Stats, and Pomodoro are one tap away. Use the Tune menu to choose which shortcuts you see.
Protection is a boundary, not a punishment

Delay App: a pause before a protected app opens.
Strict mode removes the easy exit.
Emergency uses are the planned escape hatch.
Auto-quit closes an app at the limit.
Bypass Restrictions skip schedules but are still tracked.
Focus holds Shields, Goals, and Schedules. Apps and Websites are separate surfaces, and each list only shows what you created.
This button adds any of the three tools. Long-press a card to select several at once.
A Shield stands between you and an app. Set a daily limit, add a delay, or make it strict. You can always spend an emergency use.
Goals don\'t block. They reward you for staying under a target, and they feed your XP.
A Schedule automates BLOCK or ALLOW windows by day and time. BLOCK schedules can intercept notifications.

QR and NFC tasks need a code or tag registered first.
Session HUD floats your remaining time.
Usage Glimpse shows a brief total every five minutes.
Audio Focus Intercept pauses media during an overlay.
Mindful Gateway interrupts every app that isn\'t whitelisted, even if it has no Shield. Defaults control uses, emergency, and pause behavior.
Pause Point asks for a small task before you continue. Waiting, breathing, walk, scan, slide, math, counting, typing, and more.
Reels Shield shares one daily limit across your chosen apps and presses back when it runs out. It needs accessibility.
Early Kick ejects you five minutes before a limit, so the stop is a warning instead of a surprise.
Eye Care runs the 20-20-20 rule with rest overlays you can\'t skip. Work and rest lengths are yours to set.

Bedtime history and wind-down live on the Bedtime screen.
Pomodoro keeps presets and session stats.
Grace Period can wrap past midnight with a weekly edit lock.
Tamper Protection adds an uninstall step and a PIN.
Bedtime blocks distracting apps, can wind you down, and can silence notifications. Add trusted apps to the allowlist.
Pomodoro alternates focus and rest, and can protect you from apps during a session. Save a preset for the way you actually work.
Grace Period lifts every restriction for a window you choose, up to two hours a day. Weekly Edit Lock keeps it from becoming permanent.
Lockdown blocks editing Shields, Goals, and Schedules during chosen hours. Turning it off takes a deliberate confirmation.
Alarms support text-to-speech, dismiss missions, gradual volume, and launching a wake-up app.
The numbers are yours to read.

Notification Insights recap your day and week.
Intercepted notifications feed an achievement.
Weekly and monthly summaries keep unlimited history.
App Detail can edit, pause, or delete its Shield or Goal.
This donut splits your day into Shield, Goal, and Other. Peak hours and the time profile sit right below.
The heatmap is your history at a glance. Swipe back through weeks, months, and years, and compare with last week.
Tap any app for App Detail: 21-day and hourly charts, battery, peak hour, and the Shield or Goal attached to it.
Website auto-tracking records time on domains across supported browsers, and website Shields work like app Shields.
Identity and resilience make it last
Make it yours, then keep it.

Explorer badges reward trying features. Accumulation badges grow over time. Your Path badge lives here too.
Theme, Dynamic Color, Expressive Colors, fonts, the floating tab bar, and Overlay Appearance all live here.
Auto and manual backup, restore, Smart Repair, privacy, and performance profiles. Set a backup and forget it.

Your daily dashboard for screen time, streaks, and quick access to everything Zenith offers.
Shows today\'s screen time against your daily target with a live progress bar and current streak.
Compares today with yesterday and highlights your weekly trend.
Surfaces your active Goals and Shields so you always know what is protecting your attention.
Animated usage dashboard with a wavy progress bar, streak flame badge, and Yesterday/Trend cards.
Usage history calendar (tap a bar to inspect a specific day) and an expandable Top Used Apps list.
Quick Actions row (Bedtime, Alarm, Stats, Pomodoro) and Apps/Websites tabs with active Goals & Shields.
Tap the dashboard to change your daily target, presets like 2h/4h/6h are available.
Pull down anywhere to refresh your stats.
New installs need about 3 days of data before history and trends become reliable.
The central hub for building distraction controls: app & website Shields, usage Goals, and blocking Schedules.
Shields block or gate chosen apps and websites whenever you try to open them.
Goals let apps run freely but reward staying under a usage limit with streaks and incentives.
Schedules activate shields automatically at set days and times.
Apps/Websites tabs listing Active Goals, Active Shields, and Schedules with sortable headers.
An expanding + button to add a Shield, Goal, or Schedule.
A red banner when editing is restricted by Lockdown hours.
Long-press any item to enter multi-selection mode, then long-press again to toggle more items.
Deleting requires completing the 3-lever confirmation puzzle on purpose, friction helps you reconsider.
Website shielding needs the Accessibility Service enabled.
Global preferences and the entry point to every category of Zenith\'s configuration.
Controls global behavior: screen-time target, emergency recharge, delay-app duration, day start time, and permissions.
Routes into categorized settings: Features, Appearance, Performance, Data Management, and Developer.
Handles app updates and changelog access.
A featured carousel surfacing updates and shortcuts.
General settings blocks plus one card per category.
An About section with developer-mode toggle and update options.
Updates are checked automatically on open if enabled; otherwise use the manual check button.
Bypass Restrictions and Private & Hidden Apps are managed via sheets inside General Settings.
Enable developer mode in About to unlock extra categories and tools.
Bounce you back to the home screen when a shielded app is opened while a trigger app is active.
Opening any shielded app while a trigger app is in the foreground sends you straight back home.
Whitelisted apps stay exempt, so they can still open shielded apps without being redirected.
A master toggle, an accessibility warning when the service is off, and three dedicated app lists.
Shielded Apps, Whitelisted Apps, and Trigger Apps each open a full-screen multi-app selector with search, select all, and per-app checkboxes.
Pick a few trigger apps you actually work inside, and the shield arms every time you open one.
Whitelist the launcher or a trusted app if you still need to reach a shielded app on purpose.
Zenith\'s accessibility service must stay enabled for app switches to be detected.
Deep-dive analytics of your screen time by day, hour, app, website, and focus category, plus personal insights.
Breaks usage down into Shield / Goal / Other categories and shows where your hours actually go.
Detects patterns like peak hours, efficiency score, sessions, and a time profile (e.g. Night Owl).
A donut chart per category, hourly bar chart (bedtime hours tinted), and weekly trend calendar.
Per-hour drill-down lists (\'Apps used at HH:00\') with Usage/Recent sorting.
Highlight and About You sections with heatmap, snapshot stamps, and weekly stats.
Tap a donut segment to highlight that category across the charts.
Tap any hour bar to expand its app breakdown; tap the Time Profile card to jump to your peak hour.
Pull down to refresh, with Smart Repair enabled it also recalculates inconsistent records.
A nightly mode that keeps you off distracting apps during sleep hours, gamified with streaks.
Blocks non-allowed apps during your bedtime window and counts a streak for every night you respect it.
Optional companions: wind-down notification before bed, Do Not Disturb, and pre-bed restrictions.
A large breathing countdown ring showing when bedtime ends or starts, plus weekday picker.
Current/best streak cards, a Bedtime Activity hourly chart, and History/Efficiency cards.
Settings cards for allowed apps, wind-down notification, DND, and restrictions.
Turning bedtime OFF mid-window intentionally requires the hardest confirmation (10 levers in 10 seconds).
Add trusted apps (e.g. music, phone) to Allowed Apps so they skip the bedtime block, their Shields and Goals still apply.
Tap an activity bar to see exactly which apps were used at that hour.
A full alarm clock built to get you out of bed, integrated with Zenith\'s anti-oversleep tooling.
Fires alarms with rich wake-up enforcement: pause-point dismiss missions, spoken phrases, gradual volume, and snooze limits.
Can auto-open selected \'wake up\' apps when dismissed so you start your morning routine.
Alarm cards grouped by day with name, oversized time, live countdown chip, and repeat/vibrate icons.
A sort control (Time / Name / Closest), a + button to add alarms, and a detailed edit sheet.
Today-active alarms highlight with primary-container color.
Swipe an alarm row left/right for edit and delete actions.
Long-press to enter selection mode for bulk deletion (3-lever puzzle).
Changing an alarm\'s time or days re-enables it automatically; the master switch in the header gates all alarms.
A scheduled daily window (up to 2 hours) in which every Zenith restriction is lifted, making blocking sustainable instead of absolute.
During the window, shields, schedules, and bedtime will not block any app.
Outside the window, all protections return automatically, no manual re-enabling needed.

Optional Weekly Edit Lock (off by default): when enabled, changing the window or days is limited to one change per week, and each change starts a 7-day lock on these settings only. Your app blocking is never affected.
A toggle card, a pulsing countdown ring (\'Grace period ends in…\' / \'Starts in…\'), and time pickers.
A weekday selector so the window only applies on chosen days.
A Weekly Edit Lock card (off by default) with a countdown note while it is active, and a confirmation dialog before each change that starts the lock.
Plan a realistic window (max 2 hours) and repeat days, then double-check the confirmation dialog. With the edit lock enabled, even unselecting a single day counts as the weekly change.
Wrap-around times are supported, so windows can span midnight.
Enable Weekly Edit Lock once your window is settled to protect it from impulsive edits; turning the lock back off requires the 10-lever confirmation.
Disabling the window mid-session requires the 10-lever confirmation but does not consume the weekly change; only window and days edits do.
Combine with Lockdown if you want editing protected while grace period is off.
Applies the 20-20-20 rule: after a stretch of screen time you get a short, unskippable rest overlay.
Tracks continuous usage and forces a brief rest break so your eyes can recover.
Both the work length and rest length are tunable.
A toggle card, a Work Time slider (1–60 min), and a Rest Time slider (5–60 sec).
While active, a full-screen rest overlay appears when work time expires.
Classic guidance is ~20 minutes of work followed by ~20 seconds looking away, both sliders let you adapt it.
Sliders commit on release, so drag freely until the value feels right.
The break overlay is intentionally unskippable, that\'s the point.

One shared daily limit for short videos, optional per-app limits, and an automatic back-press when a limit is reached. Apps are categorized as fully supported, partial support, or untested based on detection accuracy.
Counts short videos watched across tracked apps, with every short-video feed sharing the same daily limit.
Fully supported apps offer precise detection, whereas partial support apps may occasionally miss or over-count swipes on secondary screens like comment sections or post details.
Untested apps are tracked normally, but their detection logic has not been specifically fine-tuned.
Shares a single daily limit across all tracked apps while maintaining a per-app breakdown of today\'s videos.
Allows setting individual app limits below the shared limit, enforcing whichever limit is stricter.
Presses back automatically when opening or scrolling short videos once the shared limit or an app limit is reached.
A visual progress ring showing remaining videos, alongside stat cards for today\'s usage, active apps, total lifetime count, and shield status.
Text inputs for setting limits, including the shared daily limit and individual app caps in a per-app usage list.
A tracked-app selector and a 14-day history chart showing daily usage broken down by app.
Zenith\'s accessibility service must be active, as scroll detection requires full accessibility mode.
Detection algorithms only track short-video feeds, never home feeds, comments, or post descriptions.
Lowering the shared limit on busy days automatically tightens per-app caps. The floating overlay displays your remaining limit and current session count.
Everything about a single app: its usage, streak, limits, and the shield or goal attached to it.
Shows today\'s usage against this app\'s limit/goal, yesterday comparison, trend, and streak.
Lets you manage the app\'s Shield or Goal directly, including pausing it temporarily.
Header with the app icon (dimmed when blocked), streak badge, and SHIELD/GOAL type chip.
\'Today\'s Usage\' hero card, Yesterday/Trend stat cards, a 21-day history chart, and an hourly chart.
Battery usage, Peak Usage Hour, and Pause/Delete actions when a focus is active.
Use the pencil icon in the top bar to open this app\'s shield/goal settings sheet.
Pausing asks for a duration via the lever sheet; deleting requires the 3-lever puzzle.
Pull down to refresh the stats.
Schedule hours during which Focus-screen editing is completely blocked, protecting your controls from your future self.
During lockdown hours you cannot add, edit, or delete shields, goals, or schedules.
Disabling lockdown mid-session deliberately requires the hardest confirmation.
A toggle card and a large countdown ring (\'Lockdown starts in…\' / red \'ends in…\' while active).
Start/end time pickers, weekday selector, and a Disable Lockdown button.
Set lockdown for your most impulsive hours (e.g. late night).
Turning it on is easy on purpose; disabling takes 10 levers within 10 seconds, and time/days cannot be changed while active.
Combine with Grace Period so breaks stay planned, not improvised.
Anti-uninstall: Zenith becomes a device administrator, so Android asks for an extra step before it can be uninstalled.
Registers Zenith as a device administrator so Android requires an extra deactivation step before the app can be uninstalled.
Requires a user-set 4-8 digit PIN to turn protection off or change it.
Optionally blocks turning protection off during Lockdown hours.
A status card showing whether protection is active or whether administrator rights were revoked outside the app.
A device administrator activation prompt when enabling, and a PIN sheet for every sensitive change.
Set the PIN before you need it, it is the only way to turn protection off inside Zenith.
If Android no longer lists Zenith as an administrator, use Re-activate to restore protection.
A factory reset or deactivating the administrator in system settings cannot be blocked; Zenith warns you if it happens.
A focus timer that breaks work into sessions separated by short breaks, with optional app lockdown during sessions.
Runs repeating focus/break cycles with configurable lengths, session counts, and long-break cadence.
Optionally blocks distracting apps for the whole session, enforced behind a puzzle.
A big wavy circular countdown that changes color between session, break, and paused states.
Configuration cards for durations, sessions, App Protection toggles, and the Allowed Apps picker.
Named presets you can save, load, and delete (e.g. \'Work\', \'Study\').
Emptying the allowed-apps selection means every non-system app is blocked during sessions.
Ending a session early requires the 10-lever confirmation, commit before you start.
Pause keeps app blocking on but lets notifications through; break has a 30 min cooldown.
Requires completing a small task before a block overlay lets you through, a speed bump against mindless unblocking.
When an interception fires, a random enabled task must be completed before continuing.
You choose which task types may appear from the toggles below.
Task type cards with individual switches (waiting, breathing, walk, QR/NFC scan, number slide, switch, math, counting, typing, goal-app choice).
For QR/NFC scan: how many codes/tags are saved and a shortcut to the QR/NFC setup screens.
The header switch quickly enables/disables the whole feature.
Enable multiple task types so the challenge stays unpredictable.
If you enable QR/NFC scanning, register codes/tags first, otherwise the task cannot be satisfied.
Fewer enabled types = faster unblock, more types = stronger friction.
Your identity, lifetime top apps, activity heatmap, streak, XP level, and achievements, all computed offline.
Shows your banner, photo, name, and bio (tap the edit icons to change them).
Top 3 lifetime apps come from an incremental snapshot so the full history is never re-summed on every open.
Activity heatmap, screen time streak, and an XP level that rewards staying under shield limits and hitting goal targets.
Explorer badges for trying Zenith features and tiered accumulation badges (star, moon, sun, comet, crown, diamond, trophy).
A Share button that renders your profile to an image you can send anywhere.
XP is awarded once per day: shields pay for unused headroom, goals pay for reaching or passing the target.
Achievement tiers use custom roman numerals, collect higher tiers by growing streaks and saved time.
Every badge in one place: explorer badges for trying features and tiered accumulation badges with unlock history.
Lists all achievements grouped by Explorer and Accumulation with live progress.
Tapping a badge opens its detail: tier ladder (before, current, next) and unlock dates.
Grouped rows with progress bars and numeric targets.
Custom roman tier icons from star up to trophy.
New unlocks also pop up as a springy banner on the Profile screen.
Your XP level, level rewards, and daily XP history.
Tracks total XP and shows progress to the next level, each level needs more XP than the last.
Level milestones unlock titles and avatar borders you can equip from the card rows.
Titles from Initiate up to Infinite, and avatar rings growing from 1 solid color to a 5-color gradient.
The 5th ring of each color group is animated: Rose shines, Lagoon, Candy, Spring, and Eternity spin.
Unlocked rewards turn primary-colored; locked ones stay neutral until their level is reached.
Daily XP history with saved screen time per day.
Tap an unlocked reward to equip it, tap again to unequip.
Your equipped title also appears on the shared profile card.
Tune exactly how each Pause Point task behaves so the difficulty matches your intent.
Sliders and switches let you set the size/duration of each task type independently.
Values you choose here are what the Pause Point overlay will actually use.
A header card describing the task type.
Per-type controls, e.g. wait duration, breathing rounds, steps, grid size, math range, counting target, or the typing-text pool.
QR Scan and NFC Scan register their codes and tags right here on this screen.
Changes save instantly and apply to the next generated pause task.
If you enable QR scanning, register codes first, otherwise the task cannot be satisfied. Same for NFC tags.
Choose App uses your goal apps automatically.
Defaults match the original values, so untouched tasks behave exactly as before.
Customize how blocking and interception overlays look, with a live preview of the real thing.
Controls the color theme, transparency, and layout of the bottom-sheet overlays shown when something is blocked.
A live Preview card rendering the actual overlay for \'Example App\'.
Color Theme swatches (including Dynamic and Custom), an Opacity slider, and a Full-Screen toggle.
Watch the preview while dragging the opacity slider to find a level that\'s visible but not blinding.
Custom unlocks a hue slider for a fully personal palette.
Full-screen makes the sheet fill the display, useful if small sheets tempt you to peek around them.
Live-tune Zenith\'s variable Google Sans Flex typography, style by style.
Adjusts font axes (weight, width, etc.) per text style and previews the result instantly.
A preview card with wordmark, headline, and body samples.
Preset chips (Zenith / Neo / Impact / Airy) and a custom switch unlocking fine-grained axis sliders.
Start from a preset, then flip \'Use Custom Variable\' to fine-tune individual axes.
Use copy/save to keep configurations you like before experimenting further.
Toggle Zenith\'s behavioral modules: interface overlays, notifications, entry control, triggers, and tracking.
Interface Overlays: total usage pill, session HUD, usage glimpse, and current calendar event.
Entry Control: Mindful Gateway pauses before opening apps; Incentive Lock unlocks shields progressively as goals complete.
Triggers: pause media on overlay, Early Kick before limit, battery reset tracking; plus website auto-tracking.
Grouped sections of switches and sub-settings, with links to Grace Period, Eye Care, Pomodoro, Lockdown, and Pause Point.
Incentive Lock gives bonus uses at 25%%/50%% goal completion; disabling it starts a 1-hour countdown you can still cancel.
Early Kick ejects you from an app 5 minutes before its limit, great as a warning system.
Make Zenith yours: theme, fonts, dynamic color, expressive colors, and navigation layout.
Chooses light/dark theme, app font (including the GS Flex customizer), Dynamic Color on Android 12+, and the expressive color set.
Layout options such as the floating tab bar and overlay appearance live here too.
Theme/font selectors, toggles for Dynamic Color and Expressive Colors, and layout switches.
Dynamic Color follows your wallpaper; Expressive Colors adds livelier accents on top.
Open Overlay Appearance from here to style the blocking sheets themselves.
Balance responsiveness vs battery: preset profiles, overnight monitoring pauses, and detection tuning.
Performance Profile sets how aggressively Zenith detects app opens (higher = snappier, more battery).
Unused Hours pauses monitoring overnight; Instant Detection uses the Accessibility Service for immediate checks.
Custom Tuning exposes polling-delay sliders per context.
Selectable profile circles, unused-hours time pickers, and threshold sliders with reset buttons.
Changes here must be applied via the floating Apply Settings button before leaving, Back is intercepted until then.
If detection feels slow, raise the profile first before touching custom sliders.
Enabling Instant Detection improves accuracy but asks for the accessibility service.
Decide what Zenith may observe, store, and include in backups, with sensitive apps excluded before processing.
Private & Hidden Apps is one sheet with two levels: Private apps are fully ignored and purged; Hidden apps remain monitored but are excluded from stats.
Limited Accessibility Mode restricts the service to app-switch events only, disabling browser URL tracking and content/text inspection.
Notification privacy controls exempt apps from interception and can avoid storing message titles/body text.
A unified Private & Hidden Apps picker with Private and Hidden tabs, both available from General Settings and Privacy.
An Accessibility Mode toggle, Notification Interception controls, excluded notification apps, and a content-storage toggle.
A notification privacy explainer plus a cloud/local backup summary.
Prefer Private for banking, authenticator, health, or messaging apps; use Hidden when you only want to hide screen time without disabling monitoring.
Bypass Restrictions only skip schedules, shields, and goals; those apps are still tracked. Use Private & Hidden Apps when you want an app ignored or hidden from stats.
Turn off Store Notification Contents if you want interception without keeping message text.
Android Auto Backup excludes the usage/notification database, but local backups you create from Data Management include it, so store them privately.
Back up and restore your entire Zenith setup so nothing is lost between devices or reinstalls.
Auto Backup saves periodic snapshots (3–24h interval) to a folder you choose.
Manual Backup exports on demand; Restore brings everything back and restarts the app.
Backup & Restore card with last-backup time, interval chips, and action buttons.
Sync & Maintenance options like Sync on Entry.
Pick a cloud-synced folder (e.g. Drive) as the auto-backup location for off-device safety.
Restore shows a metadata confirmation sheet first, verify the date before proceeding.
Power tools: database editor, repair utilities, live logs, onboarding triggers, and UI test harnesses.
Edits raw records (streaks, global stats), inspects the database, and runs Smart Repair.
Re-runs onboarding flows and provides functional test surfaces (overlays, TTS, fonts).
Database Editor, Database Records viewer, System Usage Fetch, Data Repairment entries.
Live DB and Overlay log viewers plus various test launchers.
Prefer Smart Repair over manual edits unless you know exactly what you\'re changing.
Log viewers are invaluable when reporting bugs, attach their output.

Everything stays on your device. Here is what Zenith can access and where your data lives.
Detects app launches in real time. Standard mode reads window titles and active browser URLs; Limited mode requests app-switch events only.
Why it\'s needed: to detect app launches instantly so Zenith can show mindful messages and shields.
Standard mode reads window titles and active browser URLs for website monitoring. It never stores what you type or the content of your screen.

Limited mode requests ONLY app-switch events. Content-change events, text-change events, interactive window trees, and key-event filtering are not requested. Browser URL tracking and the back-key overlay shortcut stop working; mindful messages and app shields keep working.
No keylogging: Zenith never listens to or records keystrokes in either mode.
If access is revoked, instant app-launch detection, browser tracking, and the back-key shortcut stop. With Usage Stats access, Zenith falls back to polling, so shields may arrive with a delay.
Limited mode reduces what Android sends to Zenith. The Accessibility permission itself stays granted until you revoke it in Android Settings.
Optional. Pauses distracting notifications during focus sessions or schedules and can restore them afterwards.
Why it\'s needed: to pause distracting notifications during active schedules or Pomodoro sessions and optionally restore them afterwards.
Turn Notification Interception off in Privacy settings and Zenith ignores notifications even if Android notification access is still granted.
If disabled, notification pausing and post-focus restoration stop. Mindful messages and app shields are unaffected.
Content control: with Store Notification Contents off, titles and body text are never saved. Turning it off also scrubs title/body text already stored locally.
Private apps and Excluded Notification Apps are never inspected for content, silenced, or stored. Adding an app to either list deletes its stored intercepted notifications.
Notification data lives in Zenith\'s local app database. It is not encrypted at rest, but the Android app sandbox stops other apps from reading it, and Zenith never uploads it.
Disabling interception does not revoke Android notification access. Revoke it in Android Settings if you want the system permission removed entirely.
Usage history and notification logs stay on this device. Android cloud backup is blocked; local backups you create include the full database.
Local database: your usage history and notification logs live only in Zenith\'s local database on this device.
Android Cloud Backup: the system backup rules allow only two local preference files, so zenith_database is never included in Android Auto Backup or device-to-device transfers.

What Android may back up: Zenith preferences (theme, targets, private and hidden apps) and lightweight app state such as streaks, timers, and the last known daily total. Usage history and notification logs are not included.

Local backups: Manual Backup and Auto Backup in Data Management write a ZIP with the full local database (including usage history) and the settings preference file. Store those files somewhere private or disable local auto backup.
Private apps: marking an app as private deletes its stored usage rows, intercepted notifications, and shield configuration from Zenith.
Hidden exclusions remove an app from screen-time totals, history, and streaks without deleting data or stopping monitoring.
Data control: you can clear history or reset database logs anytime from Data Management settings.
Private and Hidden control what Zenith sees or counts. Bypass Restrictions only skips blocking.
Private: fully ignored; stored data is purged.
Hidden: still monitored, but excluded from usage totals, history, and streaks.
Bypass Restrictions: still tracked, but skips schedules, shields, and goals.
In short: Private & Hidden Apps control privacy and stats; Bypass Restrictions controls blocking.
